record.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:98 — Refresh is a non-atomic read-modify-write of credential.key, so concurrent bookings and the sync webhook can clobber a newer token with a stale one.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, refresh reads `credential.key` into `googleCredentials`, mutates a couple fields, then writes the *entire* `key` back via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. The new webhook `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` can concurrently update the same credential’s `key` (also writing the entire JSON). With no optimistic locking/transactions/field-level merge, concurrent updates can cause lost updates (e.g., webhook rotates/updates `refresh_token` but the refresh path overwrites it with the older `refresh_token` still present in `googleCredentials`). This is a real clobbering risk created/exposed by the diff.
